sb_prompt: DISCUSS PLANNING A FAMILY REUNION.  DRAW ON YOUR EXPERIENCES AND THOSE OF THE OTHER CALLER FOR MAKING THE NEXT GET-TOGETHER SUCCESSFUL AND MEMORABLE.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Hi, this is Sarah. Are you Lisa from the Miller family?
ParticipantB: Yes, that's me, Lisa! It's so good to hear your voice. How are things with you?
ParticipantA: I'm doing okay, just busy with work and my kids' schedules. How is your family doing?
ParticipantB: We are all doing great! The kids are growing up so fast. I was hoping you could call to talk about our family reunion.
ParticipantA: Oh, right! The one next year. I've been thinking about it a lot. When should we plan to meet?
ParticipantB: That is the big question. My husband says we need to pick a date soon because everyone has different work schedules.
ParticipantA: I understand. My boss is pretty flexible, but my son plays football on Saturdays in the fall. That might be tricky.
ParticipantB: Oh, football! That sounds tough. Maybe we could look at summer instead? Everyone usually has a little more freedom then.
ParticipantA: Summer could work. My daughter has a dance recital in July, but maybe that's just one day. What about late August?
ParticipantB: Late August sounds nice. The weather is usually still warm, but the heat of summer is gone. What do you think?
ParticipantA: I like that idea. We wouldn't need to worry about the kids being in school full time. Where do you want to meet?
ParticipantB: Well, my parents live in Ohio, but my husband's family is up in Vermont. Which spot would be better for everyone?
ParticipantA: That is hard to say. If we go to Ohio, it is cheaper for me since I live closer. But your kids might want to see the lake in Vermont.
ParticipantB: That is a great point. My kids have been begging to go skiing in Vermont. But your kids might not know anyone up there yet.
ParticipantA: True. Maybe we can pick a location in the middle? Like Indiana? That way no one has to drive too far.
ParticipantB: Indiana is a good middle ground. We can even find a nice cabin or resort there. Have you thought about what we should do during the reunion?
ParticipantA: I was thinking we could have a big barbecue outside. It is usually easier and cheaper than renting a fancy hall.
ParticipantB: I love that idea! My dad really likes grilling. He could bring his famous ribs. But we should probably have some indoor options too, just in case it rains.
ParticipantA: Good idea. We can set up a big tent. What about activities for the kids? We need to keep them busy.
ParticipantB: How about a scavenger hunt? We can hide clues around the house or the park. My oldest daughter is good at organizing games.
ParticipantA: That sounds fun! My youngest loves running around and finding things. Can we make it team-based? Like families competing?
ParticipantB: Yes! That would be great. We can split into teams so everyone works together. It gets everyone talking and laughing.
ParticipantA: I like that. We should also think about food. Besides the barbecue, should we have dessert? Maybe a cake cutting ceremony?
ParticipantB: Definitely a cake! We can have a giant sheet cake with everyone's names on it. It makes it feel special and official.
ParticipantA: I can help bake the cake if you want. I have good recipes from my mom. What about the cost? We need to be careful with money.
ParticipantB: That is important. I think we can ask everyone to chip in equally. We can put money in a digital pot or send checks ahead of time.
ParticipantA: That works for me. I can collect the money from my side of the family. How much do you think we need per person?
ParticipantB: Maybe fifty dollars each? That should cover the food, the venue, and a little something for gifts or souvenirs.
ParticipantA: Fifty dollars sounds fair. I can ask my parents if they want to contribute too. Do you have any other ideas to make it memorable?
ParticipantB: How about creating a family tree poster? We can draw it together and put it at the entrance. It helps people remember where everyone is from.
ParticipantA: That is a wonderful idea. I can draw the branches and my kids can write their names. It will be a nice keepsake for everyone.
ParticipantB: Yes! And maybe we can take a big group photo at the end. We haven't had a full family picture in years.
ParticipantA: I agree. My kids are all different ages now, so it would be good to see them together. Who will take the picture?
ParticipantB: I can bring a camera. I took a class in photography a while ago. I think I can get a good shot of everyone.
ParticipantA: That is so nice of you. I am sure we will all appreciate it. When can we meet to finalize the plans?
ParticipantB: How about next week? We can come over to my house on Tuesday evening. We can make a checklist and decide on the details.
ParticipantA: Tuesday works for me. I am usually free after work in the evening. What time should we start?
ParticipantB: How about six o'clock? It gives us time to grab a quick bite before we dive into planning.
ParticipantA: Six sounds perfect. I will make sure to be there. Do you need anything from me before we talk?
ParticipantB: No, I think we have everything covered. I just need to ask my husband to check the Vermont dates, but we can discuss that later.
ParticipantA: Okay, I will too. I will talk to my son about his football games to see if we can move the date to August.
ParticipantB: Great. I feel much better knowing we are getting it done. It will be so special to see all of us in one place.
ParticipantA: Me too. It is been years since we had everyone under one roof. I am excited to see my cousins.
ParticipantB: The kids will love it. They have been talking about their cousins constantly. Thank you for calling to organize this.
ParticipantA: You too. I will see you next Tuesday. Have a good day until then!
ParticipantB: You too! Bye, Sarah.
ParticipantA: Bye, Lisa.
